note: Apple's Logic Pro User Guide key-command tables, the authority for which keystroke is Logic's DEFAULT for a function (#1029). Each table file is the exact bytes of the one element in a `curl -s -L ` capture of that page: from `` after it, not re-encoded. `capture_sha256` is the digest of the whole capture, so a refetch can be cut the same way and compared; `table_sha256` is what Scripts/check-cgevent-keystrokes-are-apples.py re-derives from the committed file before it reads a row. `fetched` is the capture file's modification time, which is when curl wrote it. Every page carries the sentence in `preset_sentence` once, so these are the U.S. default preset's bindings, and the guard reads each named key as the kVK_ANSI_* / kVK_* virtual keycode of that key on a U.S. keyboard.
limits: Which Logic Pro version the web guide describes is not stated on these pages and was not measured; docs/canon/MANIFEST.json pins Logic 12.3 (6674), and nothing here shows the two agree.
Logic's bundle ships its own preset (Contents/Resources/Key Commands/U.S..logikcs); its bindings sit in an opaque LogicBinaryPreferences blob that nothing here decodes, so the two were not compared.
Only the four pages the CGEvent key table cites are pinned; a keystroke whose row lives on another key-command page needs that page pinned the same way first.
